result.topic_en: The page finishes an argument that every form near a form expressible as a sum of 2n-th powers of linear forms with positive coefficients is itself so expressible, then sets out a plan to prove the prime number theorem by systematically solving Chebyshev's functional equation, and begins a remark on problems such as quartic surfaces with 11 ovals.
result.transcription:
dass $\mu\nu >$ als die Anzahl der Koeffizienten einer Form $2n^{\text{ter}}$ Ordnung
wird und setze
$f = l_1^{2n} + \cdots + l_\nu^{2n} + (l_1')^{2n} + \cdots \qquad + (l_\nu^{(\mu-1)})^{2n}$
so dass $f$ durch {+$\mu\nu$+} diese Potenzen jede Form überhaupt darstellbar wird und
daher auch jede Nachbarform$_x$ in der Gestalt
$f = (1+\varepsilon_1)\, l_1^{2n} + \cdots \qquad + (1+\varepsilon_{\mu\nu})(l_\nu^{(\mu-1)})^{2n}$
wo $\varepsilon_1 \ldots \varepsilon_{\mu\nu}$ ${}^x$so klein gemacht werden können, dass $1+\varepsilon_1 \ldots 1+\varepsilon_{\mu\nu}$
auch positiv bleiben. —— Andererseits folgt auch leicht, dass
jede Form, in deren beliebiger Nähe Formen, die durch posit. Potenzen
darstellbar sind, liegen, es ebenfalls ist, etc.

items.english: On the other hand it also follows easily that every form in whose arbitrary neighbourhood there lie forms representable by positive powers is itself representable as well, etc.

Funktion und überhaupt [-einen-] neuen Beweisen für

items.english: I seek to obtain Riemann's theorem on the zeros of the zeta(s) function, and in general new proofs of the fact that the number of primes divided by (log x)/x tends to 1 as x goes to infinity, by trying to solve systematically the Chebyshev equation theta(x) + theta(x/2) + theta(x/3) + ... = log[x!] and to work out its theory.

items.english: The right-hand side log([x]!) must be represented systematically, and then the special functions theta = 1/x, log x, x^s must be substituted and treated.
